text:
Drew O'Connor is having the kind of season that puts a name in trade columns. Vancouver Hockey Daily floated him as a Canucks trade target in early November, Yardbarker called him a possible under-the-radar one, and Canucks Army wrote that Manny Malhotra "calls out Drew O'Connor's penalty troubles". On Friday against the Rangers he played 9.6 minutes, his lowest in his last ten games.

He has 2 goals and 5 points in 21 games, and not all of that is on him. He's turned 3.36 expected goals (the quality of his chances) into 2, shooting 7.4% where our range puts his true rate nearer 12.5%, and the Canucks have scored 4.57 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice. The process is better than it looks, too: Vancouver has 42.9% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, which is poor, but 4 points better than without him. The tools are still there, a 6'4" frame and top speed in the 96th percentile. The open question is how many minutes, and in which city.
headline: O'Connor's minutes are shrinking as the trade talk grows
